tools.description:
Interact with a real website loaded in the app's integrated browser: open a URL, reproduce a page (or one element) as editable canvas layers, screenshot it, or pull its DOM/screenshot back into the conversation.

Use it to iterate on real designs: import a live page onto the canvas, take inspiration from a site, or close the loop when generating a design — load the generated page, look at it, and refine.

Parameters:
- action (required):
  - "load-page": load "url" in the target browser (opening the sidebar if closed and no "nodeId" is given). Returns when the load finishes or fails.
  - "import-to-canvas": reproduce the target as editable Pencil layers on the canvas. The response reports the imported top-level frame's id for use with the execute tool. Each imported node's "context" field holds the source element's tag, prefixed with its code component name when detected (e.g. "Card - div") — useful for locating the element in the code.
  - "screenshot-to-canvas": place a screenshot of the target on the canvas as an image.
  - "return-element": return the target element's DOM and computed styles as text so you can read/reuse it.
  - "return-screenshot": return a screenshot of the target as an image so you can look at it.
- nodeId: the id of a browser node in the document to drive. When omitted, the tool drives the browser sidebar's own page. Browser nodes are canvas nodes of type "browser"; find their ids with get_app_state or batch_get.
- target (default "full-page"): what to act on.
  - "full-page": the whole page.
  - "selection": the element the user picked with the browser's element picker (errors if none).
  - "query": the element resolved from "querySelector".
- querySelector: a CSS selector, required when target is "query".
- url: an http(s) or file URL, required (and only used) when action is "load-page".

Usage:
- Call action "load-page" before the other actions so a page is loaded and visible.
- localhost dev servers usually live-reload: when the page is already loaded, skip "load-page" and check the result directly (e.g. "return-screenshot"); only if your change is not visible, reload with "load-page" and check again.
- Prefer target "query" or "selection" over "full-page" to keep imports and reads focused.
- Be careful with "return-element" on "body"/"html" or broad selectors: a whole page's DOM can be huge and overflow the context. Query a specific section (e.g. "header", ".pricing", "#hero"), or use "return-screenshot" to view the whole page cheaply.
- "return-screenshot" is for you to inspect visually; "screenshot-to-canvas" and "import-to-canvas" put the result in the user's document.
- Imported pages land as normal canvas nodes. Do NOT think in CSS/HTML afterwards — treat the result as a design and edit it with the execute tool like any other content.

Examples:
- Reproduce a hero section as editable layers: {action: "load-page", url: "https://example.com"}, then {action: "import-to-canvas", target: "query", querySelector: "header.hero"}.
- Rebuild a component faithfully: {action: "return-element", target: "query", querySelector: ".pricing-card"} to read its DOM and styles, then {action: "return-screenshot", target: "query", querySelector: ".pricing-card"} to check your own render against it.
- Close the loop on a locally served generated page: {action: "load-page", url: "http://localhost:3000"}, then {action: "return-screenshot", target: "full-page"}.

action.description: What to do: load-page, import-to-canvas, screenshot-to-canvas, return-element, or return-screenshot.

filePath.description: An optional file path to access a .pen file.

nodeId.description: Id of a browser node in the document to drive. Omit to drive the browser sidebar's own page.

querySelector.description: A CSS selector executed in the page. Required when target is "query".

url.description: An http(s) or file URL to load. Used when action is "load-page".

tools.description: Use get_app_state if you don't have execute documentation

editId.description: The id of the failed snippet to patch, as printed in that call's failure message. Send it only together with `edits`, and always use a valid editId that is referencing a failed execute call. Never send it alongside `input`.

edits.description: When an execute call fails, ALWAYS retry with this instead of resending the snippet in `input`. Each edit replaces `find` with `replace` in the failed snippet, then the patched snippet re-runs from scratch. Edits apply in order: each `find` must match the snippet as already modified by the preceding edits. Requires `editId`; omit `input` when using it. If the patched snippet fails again, keep fixing it with further `edits` under the same editId - `find` must then match the already-patched snippet.

all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring a unique match.

find.description: Exact text in the failed snippet to replace. Must match exactly once unless `all` is true.

filePath.description: An optional file path to access a .pen file.

input.description: The JavaScript snippet to execute. Required unless `edits` is provided.

tools.name: execute

tools.description:
Load visual style archetypes for working with .pen files. Styles provide configurable fonts, colors, and imagery. Styles do not save variables, they only provide reference values.

Usage:
1. get_style(): list available styles
2. get_style({ name }): load style with no params or get required params when required
3. get_style({ name, params }): load style

params.description: Key-value pairs for required params returned in step 2

tools.name: get_style

tools.description:
Read the pen-dev skill that teaches how to design on the pen.dev canvas.

Usage:
1. read_skill(): returns the skill's SKILL.md
2. read_skill({ path }): read a file referenced from SKILL.md (e.g. "execute.md", "guide/web-app.md")

path.description: Relative path of a file referenced from SKILL.md. Omit to read SKILL.md itself.

tools.name: read_skill
